findings.title: Hash-consistent normal evidence with missing, mistyped or contradictory result facts is accepted as success
findings.reachable_precondition: A record is readable and its publication/hash/length links are valid, but its result fields are missing/mistyped or disagree with the candidate/outcome. This is precisely the approved valid-hash/invalid-JSON-contract fault model. No arbitrary public JSON/HTTP authority or physical cleanup bypass is alleged.
findings.actual_call_path: actual main -> runPositivePilot -> default artifact mapper/link hashes -> verifyPublishedRun; actual legacy uses the same checker and uses accepted in root deletion. Candidate is checked only for kind/root/mode/authoritative/raw_segments_saved, not its original_failure/settlement_failure/cleanup/terminal/image. final original_failure and settlement_failure are coerced to null whenever isRecord fails, including missing/string/array. normal noExtraFailure checks only final cleanup_facts.length and snapshot.cleanup_failures===0; it does not reject snapshot.transport_failure or latched_outcome.kind=failure and does not compare candidate or outcome.cleanupFacts. Thus final missing error fields or diagnostic carrying an extra transport/latched failure can still yield reliable=true/accepted=true/exit0.
findings.contract: R5F SPEC group2 explicitly requires missing/wrong-type JSON fields and protocol inconsistencies to be unreliable3, and original result/candidate/final/outcome, terminal/settlement/diagnostic cleanup and mode-specific success to agree. Normal acceptance requires no extra failure, not only empty cleanup.
findings.minimal_fix: Validate presence and bounded types for the actual v2 result fields (explicit null versus a properly typed error), including diagnostic, image/terminal and published artifact row error fields. Do not normalize malformed/missing errors to null. Compare candidate/final normalized facts against each other and the real outcome, including raw cleanup; apply the producer's normal transport/latched failure predicate to the final diagnostic. Missing/malformed/contradictory protocol evidence must return reliable=false/accepted=false/exit3. Keep coherent ordinary failed evidence at reliable=true/accepted=false/exit1.
direct_counterexamples: Guarded normal supervisor + real temporary FS; override only writeEvidence(candidate): serialize a copy with original_failure={name:'Error',message:'candidate EIO',code:'EIO'} or cleanup_facts=[error], or delete settlement_failure/terminal_proof. Delegate the real writer. The actual producer mapper and final links naturally hash those bytes; outcome/final remain clean. Current checker accepts normal0 because it ignores those candidate result fields. Run through actual main as the decisive future test.

Guarded normal fixture; at publishEvidence serialize the actual final with diagnostic_snapshot.transport_failure=EPIPE and/or latched_outcome={kind:'failure',code:'DRAW_PROTOCOL',message:'extra failure'}, keeping cleanup_failures=0; delegate REAL publishEvidence so final digest and size are real. Current normal branch accepts0 even though the stored terminal diagnostic explicitly says failure.

Delete final.original_failure/settlement_failure or replace each with a string before real publication; all hashes agree and isRecord converts each malformed value to null. Require3, not accepted0. Separately test coherent ordinary failure1 remains1, while contradictory final.kind/exit versus outcome is protocol3 rather than ordinary1.
findings.test_gap: Actual shared checker is now tested directly, which is an improvement. Existing valid-hash mutations1770-1850 cover mode/protocol/link/length only. Existing extra-error test1660 uses a producer fixture that already judged the run failed, not a hash-consistent record with omitted or contradictory normal fields.
findings.impact: The only byte/protocol authority can green-light contradictory or incomplete mandatory evidence; main can answer0 and the actual legacy consumer can authorize root deletion. This is evidence acceptance integrity, not proof that production kernel cleanup was bypassed.
findings.runtime: NOT_RUN; pure counterexample designs/static branch evaluation only, not captured old-code failures

findings.title: Expected-fault verification accepts an unrelated settlement error and does not bind cancel provenance to the original Error
findings.reachable_precondition: A hash-consistent fault publication is submitted to the actual checker. All success-looking flags, original EXPECTED_ASSERTION_FAILURE, terminal proof, null picture and zero cleanup stay present, but settlement/cancel facts differ from the actual outcome or candidate. The same approved serialized-record fault injection can reach this through actual run/main without a live C/N.
findings.actual_call_path: verifyPublishedRun accepts any record at final.settlement_failure (2130 only !==null). It checks only originalFailure.code; cancel provenance checks accepted_as_primary/superseded flags but not error_code/error_name/message matching the original. Fault agrees never inspects outcome.originalFailure, outcome.settlementFailure or their object/cause relationship, outcome.pictureBytes or cleanupFacts. Candidate's corresponding errors are never compared. Therefore final settlement_failure={name:'Error',message:'unrelated failure',code:'EPIPE'} or even {} still accepted:true/exit1 while outcome/candidate preserve the original expected error.
findings.contract: R5F SPEC group2 requires the exact EXPECTED_ASSERTION_FAILURE and same original cancellation/settlement with no extra error. The producer judge:1514 actually verifies settlementFailure===originalFailure or settlementFailure.cause===originalFailure; replacing it with non-null serialized evidence is explicitly weaker. In-memory original Error identity must not be reconstructed from a JSON code alone.
findings.minimal_fix: For fault, verify the actual outcome's original deliberate Error and settlement object/cause relationship, compare the normalized bounded originals/settlement in candidate/final to the real outcome, and bind all cancel provenance error fields to that original. Validate null actual image/byte fields and raw cleanup consistently. If the protocol needs a private producer-issued relation fact to preserve wrapper cause information, add a narrowly bound fact rather than inferring identity from strings; original outcome already carries the real objects. Reject record/outcome contradictions with unreliable3; a well-formed ordinary failure remains not accepted/exit1.
direct_counterexamples: Use the existing guarded silent fault fixture and real temp FS. Override only publishEvidence for final: copy final and replace settlement_failure with an unrelated EPIPE error record (or {}). Delegate real atomic publisher; returned final hash/size match actual bytes, candidate/outcome still have the deliberate original Error. Call actual verifyPublishedRun and main. Current logic yields accepted=true/exit1; require protocol3/no acceptance.

Keep final.original_failure.code=EXPECTED_ASSERTION_FAILURE but set cancel_provenance.error_code='OTHER', error_name/message to a different error, leaving the two accepted/superseded booleans and latched DRAW_CANCELLED intact. Current checker accepts; require mismatch refusal.

On a legitimate published fault, pass an otherwise identical internal outcome carrying a different originalFailure/settlementFailure, or non-null pictureBytes/extra cleanupFacts. Existing fault agrees ignores those fields. Add wrong-cause and valid-wrapper-cause controls so a fix does not reject the producer's legitimate exact-cause case.
findings.test_gap: The accepted-fault test:1622 exercises only the happy path. Extra-failure test:1657 injects transport failure before producer judgement and therefore receives kind=failed; it cannot prove independently that the checker validates same settlement/cancel facts in a valid-hash fault-observed record.
findings.impact: A hash-consistent record explicitly describing an unrelated settlement/cancel can be certified as the deliberate fault. Matching outer exit1 alone cannot fix that semantic false acceptance. No claim of a new raw-signal/resource-owner defect.
